spec.prompt:
CAMERA: copy EXACTLY the isometric camera of the two attached reference assets: every building is seen from a corner, showing TWO facades that both recede diagonally (front facade on the left side going up-left, side facade on the right side going up-right), the nearest vertical corner of the building points toward the viewer at the bottom centre. Never draw a building seen straight from the front. The references only show the camera angle and level of detail — do NOT copy their buildings.
SIGNS: spell every sign EXACTLY as written between quotes, letter by letter, Portuguese with accents and the tilde (São, Graça, Administração).
Asset sheet of the whole 'Xipuli' neighbourhood of Huambo, Angola. Every public building carries a clearly readable Portuguese sign. Draw ALL of these as separate isolated assets, in this order (left to right, top to bottom):
BIG NAMED BUILDINGS (each with its sign): (1) 'Escola Primária do Xipuli' - single-storey school building with a covered veranda and the Angolan flag on a pole; (2) 'Centro de Saúde do Xipuli' - white and light-blue health centre with a red cross; (3) 'Igreja Católica do Xipuli' - church with a bell tower and a cross; (4) 'Mercado do Xipuli' - covered market hall with a zinc roof and fruit stalls inside; (5) 'Cantina do Xipuli' - small grocery shop (cantina) with a hand-painted sign and soft-drink adverts; (6) 'Farmácia Xipuli' - small pharmacy with a green cross; (7) 'Administração do Xipuli' - small administration office with the Angolan flag; (8) 'Churrasqueira Xipuli' - grill restaurant with plastic tables under a canopy and a charcoal grill; (9) 'Discoteca Xipuli' - night club with a neon sign and dark facade; (10) 'Prédio Xipuli' - four-storey apartment block with balconies and water tanks on the roof; (11-19) 9 DIFFERENT family houses of the bairro: modest adobe-brick and cement-block houses with corrugated zinc roofs held by stones, small yards with reed fences, a few unfinished houses.
THEN SMALL PROPS (about 85 items, each isolated): 10 trees (jacarandas in bloom, eucalyptus, palm trees, mulemba fig, mango, avocado, bougainvillea); 6 street lamps; 4 wooden electricity poles; 2 blue-and-white candongueiro minibuses; 4 kupapata motorbikes; 3 cars; 6 zungueira and market stalls; 4 waste containers; 4 benches; 3 rooftop water tanks; 2 generators; 2 bus-stop shelters; 4 flower pots; 3 bicycles; 4 piles of cement blocks; 2 wheelbarrows; 3 yellow jerrycans; 3 chickens; 2 goats; 2 street signs reading 'Xipuli'; 2 Angolan flags on poles; 3 mobile-phone credit kiosks; 2 sacks of charcoal; 1 public water tap; 2 plastic table sets; 2 gas cylinders; 1 wooden cart; 2 walls with gates.
Every item fully separated by transparent space so each one can be cut out automatically.
